title: Star formation in 'the Brick': ALMA reveals an active protocluster in the Galactic centre cloud G0.253+0.016
question: Investigate the 'maser core' in the Galactic Centre cloud G0.253+0.016 ('the Brick') to search for active star formation, protostellar fragmentation, outflows, and precursors to high-mass stars.

data.sensitivity: Continuum: ~50 uJy beam^-1 (0.07 K); Line (in 0.78 km s^-1 channel): ~850 uJy beam^-1 (1.25 K)

what.value: Distance to Galactic Centre / G0.253+0.016 of 8.1 kpc

evidence.quote: The distance is assumed to be 8.1 kpc (cite: Gravity19; Reid_2019).

what.value: Dust opacity kappa_0 = 0.9 cm^2 g^-1 at 230 GHz and spectral index beta = 1.75

evidence.quote: Using the dust column density map from Hi-GAL (cite: higal; Cara_higal; Mills17), we estimate this mass to be $\sim$ 7$\times$10$^{3}$ M$_{\odot}$ within a radius of 19$^{\prime}$$^{\prime}$.
To measure this velocity dispersion, we take an averaged spectrum across our ALMA field using the HNCO emission from the MALT90 survey (cite: MALT90_1).

what.value: HCO+ absorption cube for comparison with 13CO filaments

evidence.quote: Inspection of the HCO$^{+}$ cube reveals that the two prominent broad-line absorption filaments shown in Figure 1 of (cite: Bally14) directly cross the centre of our ALMA field and coincide with the arcuate $^{13}$CO structures, both in position and velocity.

what.value: Volume density (1-3 x 10^6 cm^-3) and dust temperature (50-20 K) of the maser core on 1'' scales

evidence.quote: For the ‘maser core’ on 1$^{\prime}$$^{\prime}$ scales, (cite: Jill_pdf_2014) estimate a range of densities from 1 – 3$\times$10$^{6}$ cm$^{-3}$, for a dust temperature range of 50 – 20 K, respectively.

recipe.goal: Identify continuum sources and measure their sizes and integrated fluxes
recipe.method: Compute hierarchical dendrograms on the 230 GHz continuum image (robust = 0.5) using astrodendro to identify leaves as compact continuum cores, and perform a 2D Gaussian fit on the double-peaked central source #1 to decompose it into #1a and #1b.
key_parameters: threshold = 3 sigma, increment = 1 sigma, minimum number of pixels = 100 (where sigma ~ 50 uJy beam^-1)

recipe.goal: Estimate continuum core masses and volume densities
recipe.method: Calculate core masses from integrated 1.3 mm continuum fluxes using Equation 1 for optically thin dust emission, and derive volume number densities.
assumptions: Dust opacity kappa_0 = 0.9 cm^2 g^-1 at 230 GHz and beta = 1.75
Dust temperature T = 22 K (and 167 K / 120 K for internally heated sources #1a / #1b)

recipe.goal: Identify molecular outflows and derive outflow physical and energetic properties
recipe.method: Integrate SiO (5-4) emission over blue- and red-shifted velocity ranges to identify bipolar outflow lobes, calculate projected lengths, dynamical timescales, SiO column densities following Li et al. (2019), and sum over spatial and velocity extents to compute outflow masses, mass outflow rates, momenta, and kinetic energies; compare total outflow kinetic energy to local gravitational and turbulent energies.
key_parameters: Blue-shifted integration range 29 - 42 km s^-1 and red-shifted 43 - 56 km s^-1 for overview map; individual lobe velocity ranges in Table 4
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), optically thin SiO emission, and outflows parallel to the plane of the sky
Mean molecular weight mu = 2.8 and fractional SiO abundance X_SiO = 10^-8
Driving source systemic velocity v_lsr = 40 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Model gas temperature of central cores #1a and #1b using CH3CN
recipe.method: Simultaneously fit a single-component model to the beam-averaged spectrum of CH3CN (J=12-11, k=0-8) and CH3(13)CN (k=0-6) emission towards sources #1a and #1b using XCLASS within CASA.
assumptions: Beam filling factor = 1, and thermalisation between gas and dust (T_dust = T_gas) at high densities (~10^7-8 cm^-3)

recipe.goal: Estimate dynamical masses of central binary sources #1a and #1b
recipe.method: Use gravitational-kinetic energy balance on the binary separation and CH3CN 1st-moment velocity difference between sources #1a and #1b across inclination angles 15 deg <= i <= 90 deg.
key_parameters: Binary separation = 1150 AU, velocity difference = 1.5 km s^-1, inclination i = 15 to 90 deg
assumptions: Bound binary system with equal-mass components

recipe.goal: Evaluate thermal and turbulent Jeans fragmentation
recipe.method: Compute thermal Jeans mass (Equation 5), turbulent Jeans mass (substituting velocity dispersion for sound speed), and thermal Jeans length (Equation 6), and compare with observed core masses and mean projected nearest-neighbour separations.
key_parameters: Parent core density 1 - 3 x 10^6 cm^-3 and dust temperature 50 - 20 K; velocity dispersion 4 - 12 km s^-1 (large scale) or 1.5 km s^-1 (small scale CH3CN)

answer_key.quantity: Number of detected continuum sources

evidence.quote: We detect a population of eighteen continuum sources (median mass $\sim$ 2 M$_{\odot}$), nine of which are driving bi-polar molecular outflows as seen via SiO (5-4) emission.
The ‘maser core’ region fragments significantly on 1000 AU scales, revealing a small cluster of at least 18 compact sources that are detected in the dust continuum.

answer_key.quantity: Median continuum core mass

evidence.quote: Taking the aforementioned assumptions, we find that the sources range in mass from $\sim$ 0.6 – 64 M$_{\odot}$, with a median of 2 M$_{\odot}$.

answer_key.quantity: Individual continuum core mass range (excluding full central clump #1)

evidence.loc: There are no high-mass protostars in G0.253+0.016’s ‘maser core’ ... yet
evidence.quote: The mass range of the detected cores is 0.6 – 9.6 M$_{\odot}$ with a median of 2 M$_{\odot}$, though this is subject to several caveats, particularly due to uncertain dust temperatures and missing flux (see section 3.1).

answer_key.quantity: Integrated flux of central clump Source #1
Mass of central clump Source #1 (at 22 K)
Integrated flux of Source #1a
Mass of Source #1a (for T = 167 K to 22 K)
Integrated flux of Source #1b
Mass of Source #1b (for T = 120 K to 22 K)
Envelope mass of central source #1 (subtracting #1a and #1b, at 22 K)

evidence.quote: Subtracting the flux contributed by the embedded sources #1a & b, the enveloping mass is $\sim$ 35 M$_{\odot}$ (assuming T$_{\textrm{dust}}$ = 22 K), which is 16 – 100 times greater than the thermal Jeans mass.

answer_key.quantity: Number of detected bipolar SiO (5-4) outflows

evidence.quote: We detect a population of eighteen continuum sources (median mass $\sim$ 2 M$_{\odot}$), nine of which are driving bi-polar molecular outflows as seen via SiO (5-4) emission.
Overall we identify outflow signatures associated with sources #1 (a & b), #2, #4, #5, #8, #9, #11, #14, and #16.

answer_key.quantity: Outflow dynamical timescales
Outflow mass per lobe range
Outflow momentum per lobe range

evidence.quote: The estimated momenta range $\sim$ 0.1 – 12 M$_{\odot}$ km s$^{-1}$. and energies range $\sim$ 0.5 – 100 M$_{\odot}$ km$^{2}$ s$^{-2}$ (1$\times$10$^{44}$ – 2$\times$10$^{45}$ erg) per lobe.

answer_key.quantity: Outflow kinetic energy per lobe range
Mass outflow rate per lobe range
Total kinetic energy in detected outflows

evidence.quote: The total estimated energy contained in the detected outflows is $\sim$ 8$\times$10$^{45}$ erg.

answer_key.quantity: Gravitational energy of material in the ALMA field

evidence.quote: This corresponds to a gravitational energy of 5$\times$10$^{48}$ erg via $\textrm{E}_{\textrm{grav}}$ = GM$^{2}$/R.

answer_key.quantity: Turbulent energy of material in the ALMA field

evidence.quote: Using this range we estimate the turbulent energy to be $\sim$ 4$\times$10$^{48}$ – 3$\times$10$^{49}$ erg.

answer_key.quantity: CH3CN gas temperature of Source #1a

evidence.quote: The best-fitting parameters for the gas temperature, column density, and line-width are 167 K, 8.9$\times$10$^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$, and 3.6 km s$^{-1}$, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: CH3CN column density of Source #1a

evidence.quote: The best-fitting parameters for the gas temperature, column density, and line-width are 167 K, 8.9$\times$10$^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$, and 3.6 km s$^{-1}$, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: CH3CN line-width of Source #1a

evidence.quote: The best-fitting parameters for the gas temperature, column density, and line-width are 167 K, 8.9$\times$10$^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$, and 3.6 km s$^{-1}$, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: CH3CN gas temperature of Source #1b

evidence.quote: We also estimate the average gas temperature of #1b to be 120 K, using the same method.

answer_key.quantity: Dynamical mass of each central binary component (#1a, #1b) for 15 deg <= i <= 90 deg

evidence.loc: Dynamical masses of the central sources 1a & b
evidence.quote: For 15$^{\circ}$ $\leq$ *i* $\leq$ 90$^{\circ}$, the estimated dynamical mass range is 5.6 M$_{\odot}$ $\geq$ M$_{\textrm{dyn}}$ $\geq$ 1.5 M$_{\odot}$.

answer_key.quantity: Thermal Jeans mass of the maser core

evidence.quote: Taking this range of parameters, the resulting thermal Jeans mass ranges from 0.35 – 2.15 M$_{\odot}$.

answer_key.quantity: Thermal Jeans length of the maser core

evidence.quote: Taking the same range of densities and temperatures as for the Jeans mass estimation, we obtain a range of 0.8 – 1.4$\times$10$^{4}$ AU for the thermal Jeans length.

answer_key.quantity: Mean projected nearest-neighbour separation of continuum sources

evidence.quote: Using a nearest neighbour algorithm, we find that the mean projected separation of the continuum sources in our ALMA field is 4.5$\times$10$^{4}$ AU.
If we restrict this to only consider the sources in the central region of the field (sources 1 – 11), this reduces slightly to 3.4$\times$10$^{4}$ AU.

Isotopic ratio 12C/13C assumed or fitted in XCLASS when simultaneously fitting CH3CN and CH3(13)CN
missing_for_reproduction: Spatial regions/polygons used to integrate each SiO outflow lobe in Table 4
Exact tclean imaging parameters (cell size, imsize, multiscale scales, cleaning thresholds)

score_reason: Final calibrated/imaged data products are publicly hosted on Harvard Dataverse alongside raw data in the ALMA archive, and the dendrogram, dust mass, outflow, and Jeans equations and parameters are clearly specified; only minor region-definition details (outflow lobe polygons and exact tclean/XCLASS settings) are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Raw data and processed data products are public, the core catalog (Table 3), outflow properties (Table 4), CH3CN temperature fits, and Jeans fragmentation numbers are quantitative, and the analysis steps (astrodendro, dust mass equation, XCLASS, Jeans analysis) are straightforward to re-run.
